# Judith Chapter 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_006_page_001.jpg

---

**6:1** When the commotion among the men surrounding the council had subsided, Holofernes, the commander-in-chief of the Assyrian army, said to Achior and to all the Moabites in the presence of the whole assembly of foreign peoples:

**6:2** "Who are you, Achior, and you mercenaries of Ephraim, that you have prophesied among us as you did today, telling us not to make war against the people of Israel because their God will shield them? And who is god but Nebuchadnezzar? He will send his power and wipe them off the face of the earth, and their God will not save them.

**6:3** But we his servants will strike them as one man, and they cannot withstand the force of our cavalry.

**6:4** We will overwhelm them; their mountains will be drunk with their blood and their plains filled with their dead. Not even their footprints will survive before us — they shall perish utterly. So declares King Nebuchadnezzar, lord of all the earth. For he has spoken, and none of his words shall be without effect.

**6:5** As for you, Achior, hireling of Ammon, who have spoken these words in your wickedness — you shall not see my face from this day forward, until I have taken vengeance on this people that came out of Egypt.

**6:6** Then the iron of my army and the multitude of my troops shall pierce your sides, and you will fall among their slain when I return.

**6:7** Now my servants will take you off into the hill country and place you in one of the mountain towns.

**6:8** You will not perish until you are destroyed along with them.

**6:9** If you really believe in your heart that they will not be captured, then do not be downcast. I have spoken, and not one of my words shall prove false."

**6:10** Then Holofernes commanded his attendants who were standing in his tent to seize Achior, escort him to Bethulia, and hand him over to the Israelites.

**6:11** His servants seized him and brought him outside the camp into the plain, and from the middle of the plain they traveled into the hill country and arrived at the springs below Bethulia.

**6:12** When the men of the city saw them on the top of the hill, they took up their weapons, went out of the city to the crest of the hill, and all the slingers kept them at bay with stones, preventing them from going up.

**6:13** The soldiers went under the hill and bound Achior, leaving him at the foot of the hill, then returned to their master.

**6:14** The Israelites came down from their city, found him, untied him, and brought him into Bethulia, presenting him before the leaders of their city,

**6:15** who at that time were Uzziah son of Micah, of the tribe of Simeon, Chabris son of Gothoniel, and Charmis son of Melchiel.

**6:16** They called together all the elders of the city; all the young men and the women also assembled. They stood Achior in the midst of all the people, and Uzziah questioned him about what had happened.

**6:17** He answered and reported to them the proceedings of Holofernes' council, and all the words he had spoken in the assembly of the leaders of the Assyrians, and all the great boasts Holofernes had uttered against the house of Israel.

**6:18** Then the people fell down and worshiped God, crying out:

**6:19** "O Lord God of heaven, behold their arrogance, and have mercy on the humiliation of our people, and look this day with favor upon the faces of those who are consecrated to you."

**6:20** Then they comforted Achior and praised him highly.

**6:21** Uzziah took him from the assembly to his own home and gave a banquet for the elders. And they called upon the God of Israel for help throughout that night.
